result:
Done. Summary:

**Root cause:** `preflight-guard.py`'s `check_crontab_unauthorized_change()` check itself was working exactly as designed (verified via its own test suite, all 4 cases pass). The real bug was in the dispatch layer — `worker-entrypoint.sh` and `doc-worker-entrypoint.sh` classify preflight rejections into a "hard stop" list (checkpoint `blocked`, service disabled) vs. a fallthrough "transient" list (checkpoint `failed`, systemd retries). `crontab_unauthorized_change` was missing from the hard-stop list, so a deterministic, retry-proof rejection (pure function of live crontab + snapshot + this task's own unchanged prompt.txt) fell through to the transient branch, burning 9 identical restarts before the task's checkpoint history hit its lifetime cap — exactly the same bug class already fixed once for `tight_task_schema_violation` on 2026-07-23, just never extended to this later-added reason.

**Fix (PR #104):** pulled both entrypoint scripts into the repo (previously live-only), added `crontab_unauthorized_change` to both hard-stop lists, and added `tests/preflight_guard_hardstop_test.sh` which extracts the real preflight block from each live script and evals it against a faked preflight-guard.py to prevent regression. Verified no regressions in existing tests.

**known_fixes row registered:** `signature="PRE-FLIGHT REJECTED (crontab_unauthorized_change, transient)"`, `fix_action=hardstop_crontab_unauthorized_change`, `success_count=1` — matches the naming convention of the existing `hardstop_tight_task_schema_violation` row for the same bug class, so this signature will auto-resolve via watchdog step_2 going forward.

Task checkpointed `pending_review`; fix ships live via the normal PR merge → `sync-repos.sh` → `deploy-live-scripts.sh` path (deliberately not hand-deployed to `/opt/veridian/scripts/` directly, to avoid pushing unmerged code straight to production).
